results.title: Russell Says Mercedes Have Solved His Power Problems Mystery
results.description: British driver George Russell yesterday claimed that Mercedes have found the cause of his car’s power management problems and dismissed all suggestions that the team favour Kimi Antonelli. Speaking to reporters ahead of this weekend’s Hungarian Grand Prix, Russell said the team had found something that was “embedded in the calibration” of a code in his car’s power unit management that had resulted in him losing speed. The problem undermined him at last Sunday’s Belgian Grand Prix where he lost power on the opening lap and collided with former team-mate seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton of Ferrari. Antonelli went on to win the race and move 50 points clear of Russell, now in third place, in the drivers’ championship while Hamilton battled on to finish fourth and move into second, 45 points behind the Italian teenager. “There was just something deeply embedded in the calibration of the code,” said Russell. “I mean, it’s almost impossible to see unless you knew exactly what to look for. “So, I’m glad we have found it. results.title: Appeal Set In Fatal Highway Crash Case
results.description: The Fifth High Criminal Appeals Court set August 5 to hear the appeal of a driver sentenced to two years in prison for causing a traffic accident that killed one person and injured another. Prosecutors said the defendant failed to exercise proper care while driving a company vehicle on Shaikh Khalifa bin Salman Highway near Saar on May 4, 2026. The collision occurred after a broken-down vehicle had stopped in the emergency lane and a tow truck driver arrived to assist. Despite seeing the two men ahead, the defendant allegedly failed to slow down, stop or change lanes, striking both victims. One later died from his injuries, while the other was injured. The crash also caused damage to the company vehicle.

results.title: New Car Sale Cancelled After Repeated Defects
results.description: The High Civil Court of Appeal cancelled the sale of a new car after ruling that persistent technical defects made the vehicle unsafe and unreliable. The court ordered the dealership to refund BD7,000 to the buyer after deducting BD1,675 for the vehicle’s use and instructed the buyer to return the car. The dealership was also ordered to pay court costs and legal fees. According to lawyer Hameed Al Sammak, the buyer experienced repeated faults, including display screen failures, transmission issues, and an airbag system defect, despite taking the vehicle to the service centre more than 12 times. The appeal court ruled that the recurring defects during the warranty period justified cancelling the sales contract.

results.title: Oil Prices Surge Amid Middle East Escalation
results.description: London: Oil prices climbed significantly as a new escalation in the Middle East fuelled concerns about interruptions to fuel supplies and shipping routes in the region. The spike came as markets responded to growing concerns that the war could spread and endanger crucial energy infrastructure or the transit of oil through key waterways. The Middle East accounts for a significant amount of global oil production, so any threat to supplies is especially sensitive for energy markets. The rise in crude prices might increase fuel costs for individuals and businesses, adding to global inflationary pressures. Investors are eagerly monitoring developments for signs of a larger regional conflict, which may further disrupt global energy supply.
